newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 25.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on June 25. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Suharto has urged the nation's cooperatives to stay away from political issues and concentrate on economic development to increase the people's welfare.
Interior Minister Yogie Memet said violations of the rules and laws in last month's election must be followed up by the official supervision committee.
Indonesia's most prominent economist Sumitro Djojohadikusumo has expressed concern that the country's economic reforms have lost momentum at a time when many sectors badly need reforms.
The Gunung Agung group has sued another company PT Jagata for $612 million over a dispute over a purchase agreement for the debt-ridden Bank Arta Prima.

Indonesia's parliament is considering revising its internal rules to accomodate the small number of legislators from the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) following the drastic drop in the party's vote at last month's election.
The government's investment board has said the Gunawan group will build two steel mills worth 6.72 trillion rupiah in Riau and East Java provinces.
